mountpleasant.summary: Cleary describes growing up Filipino American in Massachusetts, joining the Marine Corps, and opening and running her restaurant in Washington while promoting Filipino cuisine. The archive tags the interview to Mount Pleasant.

stadiumarmory.title: Patrick Crowley
stadiumarmory.summary: Crowley saw the poor condition of Congressional Cemetery while walking his Saint Bernard in the 1990s and helped start the volunteer effort among dog walkers to improve the grounds, then joined its board. He describes the cemetery's history, geography and preservation.
stadiumarmory.archive: Ruth Ann Overbeck Capitol Hill History Project

stadiumarmory.title: Clarence Rice, M.D.
stadiumarmory.summary: Interviewed specifically about Congressional Cemetery, Rice, an Eastern High graduate of 1912 and later a pathologist, ranged wider: crossing the Anacostia as a boy, band concerts, trolley rides, and medical facilities including Gallinger Hospital.
stadiumarmory.archive: Ruth Ann Overbeck Capitol Hill History Project

trinidad.title: Joe Rose interview, 2022
trinidad.summary: Rose reflects on growing up when education, jobs and recreation were limited for Deaf Washingtonians, and on the organizations they built for themselves. He talks about Kendall School and Gallaudet College and their teachers. Conducted in American Sign Language with a voice interpreter.

trinidad.title: Gerald Miller interview, 2023
trinidad.summary: Among the first Black students admitted to the Kendall School after integration, Miller talks about childhood in Washington, his Deaf brother, his teachers, and his neighborhood before and after the killing of Martin Luther King Jr. His mother was among the parents who sued for Black Deaf schooling in the city.
trinidad.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience)

trinidad.title: Lavonda Miller interview, 2023
trinidad.summary: Among the first Black students at the Kendall School after integration, Miller explores how she communicated as a Deaf child in a hearing family and with Black and white Deaf peers, her changing awareness of race, and life after school.
trinidad.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience)

trinidad.title: Justin Miller interview, 2023
trinidad.summary: Born in 1950 not far from Gallaudet, Miller recounts his transfer to Kendall School, his teachers, communication at home, the Deaf community, music and sports, his career at The Washington Post, and his mother's struggle to secure education at Kendall.
trinidad.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience)

trinidad.title: Kenneth Miller interview, 2023
trinidad.summary: Miller describes his time at the Kendall School, his struggles with communication and hearing loss, his family's changing dynamics, the school's varied student body and the impact of its teachers.
trinidad.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience)

trinidad.title: Clifford Ogburn interview, 2023
trinidad.summary: Deaf from age three, Ogburn was sent to a segregated Maryland school because Kendall had stopped enrolling Black Deaf children in 1905. After the Miller lawsuit he and others entered Kendall in a segregated classroom. He later spent 37 years with the Postal Service in New York.
trinidad.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience)

trinidad.title: Ivy City History Booklet and oral history audio documentary
trinidad.summary: Empower DC's Ivy City page offers a history booklet, zines and an audio documentary from its oral history project. The files sit on Google Drive and we did not open them; this entry rests only on the Empower DC page.

woodleypark.title: Woodley Park Community: A Sketch of Our Past, chapter 2
woodleypark.summary: A community association history that quotes residents it interviewed in the early 1990s. One recalls telephoning the Connecticut Avenue grocer for delivery in the 1930s. Another remembers 1940s teenagers crawling under the Swiss embassy fence to build a sledding run.

woodleypark.title: Woodley Park Community: A Sketch of Our Past, chapter 3
woodleypark.summary: Quotes a former Shoreham manager on $6 rooms and a hotel run like a self-contained village with its own bakery, and a resident's memory of the delicatessen counter and summer dancing on the Shoreham terrace. Its interview notes date from 1992, and Oyster School students took part in one.

brightwood.title: Bobbie Coles interview, 2017-04-22
brightwood.summary: Coles's family moved to Van Buren Street in 1957 and faced harassment and threats as one of the first Black households in the neighborhood. At Paul Junior High, then mostly white, she was tracked for non-college-bound students; at Coolidge High she was tracked for college prep.
brightwood.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

brightwood.title: Phylicia Fauntleroy Bowman interview, 2017-07-12
brightwood.summary: Bowman's family moved to Brightwood when she was about six, the second Black family on the block. She talks about growing up on Ingraham Street, DC public schools before and after desegregation, how the neighborhood changed, and her career as an economist.
brightwood.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

brightwood.title: Joe Hairston interview, 2016-11-15
brightwood.summary: The Army's first Black helicopter pilot bought a house on Kennedy Street NW in 1954, in what had been an exclusively white neighborhood. He discusses integrating the block and his daughters' experiences in newly integrated schools, before the family moved to Shepherd Park.
brightwood.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

brightwood.title: Herbert Freeman interview, 2018-01-04
brightwood.summary: A barber who came from North Carolina in 1962 and opened Freeman's House of Styles in Brightwood Park in 1976. He discusses segregation in the South, violence against Black people then and now, the 1968 riots, and his long career.
brightwood.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Real World History Oral History Project)

congressheights.title: Michael 'Funky Ned' Neal interview, 2021-11-02
congressheights.summary: The pioneering Rare Essence bassist talks about go-go's origins in his Congress Heights neighborhood, learning from Chuck Brown at the Maverick Room, and working with his mother, who managed the band.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Go-Go Museum and Cafe Collection)

congressheights.title: Brenda Richardson interview, 2020-12-01
congressheights.summary: Richardson's family came from El Paso in 1969, and she attended Ballou High School. She became a social worker and executive director of the Anacostia-Congress Heights Partnership for the Prevention of Homelessness, and she also talks about volunteering on the Anacostia River.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Real World History Oral History Project)

congressheights.title: Mary Staton interview, 2022-11-28
congressheights.summary: Staton grew up on a North Carolina farm and protested as a student in the civil rights movement. She recounts her move to the DC area and her church community at Rehoboth Baptist Church in Congress Heights.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Real World History Oral History Project)

congressheights.title: Fred Craig interview, 2020-10-26
congressheights.summary: Craig grew up in Parkland, across from Oxon Run Parkway, and hiked the nearby forests until he was 25. He graduated from Ballou in 1968, and he talks about wild plants, leading youth camping trips, and caring for nature as a matter of faith.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

congressheights.title: Nathan Harrington interview, 2020-07-01
congressheights.summary: The founder of the Ward 8 Woods Conservancy has been active in the ward since 2009, chairing the Committee to Restore Shepherd Parkway and managing the Ward 8 Farmers Market. He talks about confronting his own fear of Ward 8 and about environmental injustice.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

congressheights.title: Kathy Elaine Senior interview, 2016-01-16
congressheights.summary: A registered nurse who trained at Freedmen's Hospital and spent 27 years at St. Elizabeths. She reflects on growing up in Columbus, Georgia, her career, and her activism in Washington.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Real World History Oral History Project)

congressheights.title: Martin Walker interview, 2022-10-13
congressheights.summary: Walker lived in Congress Heights until he was six, then moved to Landover. He talks about becoming homeless after falling behind on bills, and his 17 years with Street Sense Media as vendor, trainer, manager and board member.
congressheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

takoma.title: Carolivia Herron interview, 2017-08-11
takoma.summary: The author of Peacesong DC moved with her parents to Takoma in the early 1950s. She recounts growing up a Black Jewish kid, her family's role in blockbusting in Takoma, and Neighbors, Inc., of which the archive says she is president.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

takoma.title: Faith Wheeler interview, 2021-10-30
takoma.summary: Wheeler moved here in 1978, drawn to a mostly Black, integrated, friendly community. As an ANC commissioner, she worked on conflicts over the use of a public park, and she describes a street festival that brought park regulars together with homeowners and business owners.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

takoma.title: Joe Hairston interview, 2016-11-15
takoma.summary: Hairston moved to Shepherd Park in 1963 and joined Neighbors, Inc. to oppose blockbusting and racial steering. He reflects at length on the group's founding and its later work to stop freeways through DC and to calm traffic.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Mapping Segregation in Washington DC)

takoma.title: Layne Garrett interview, 2021-06-05
takoma.summary: The Takoma-based musician and instrument builder describes starting Rhizome DC in 2015 with five Takoma Park residents, who met through unschooling their children. It gave experimental music a home around the time Union Arts was displaced.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

takoma.title: Bobby Hill interview, 2021-06-05
takoma.summary: The longtime WPFW host co-founded Transparent Productions in 1997, and its jazz shows had been at Rhizome DC in Takoma Park for five years. He talks about how the space's indoor and outdoor rooms suited those concerts.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

takoma.title: Laura Irene interview, 2021-06-05
takoma.summary: The Mexican American artist and curator recalls Day of the Dead altars at Rhizome DC and moving performances to its big backyard during the pandemic. She also suggests how the space could better include people of color.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

takoma.title: Thomas Stanley interview, 2021-06-20
takoma.summary: The Sun Ra scholar traces his path through Black liberation movements to the arts, and how Rhizome DC gave him confidence in his artistic practice. He says it is a community, not just a building, and that the community will live on.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (DC Oral History Collaborative)

takoma.title: Deacon Clarence Haywood interview, 2020-01-05
topics: New Bethel Church of God in Christ
takoma.summary: A deacon for over three decades at New Bethel Church of God in Christ in Takoma Park, DC. He came from Camilla, Georgia, after Navy service and had a 40-year nursing career. The record's summary mostly covers his life beyond Takoma.
takoma.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Real World History Oral History Project)

deanwood.title: Brenda Walker interview, 2024
deanwood.summary: A longtime rink manager who grew up on 52nd Street NE in the Deanwood area, in a family of skaters. She talks about the Branch Avenue rink, mentoring young people, and pushing to keep the National Arena on Kalorama Road open in the 1980s.
deanwood.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (All Skate D.C.)

16thstreetheights.title: Corcoran Holt interview, 2022-08-11
topics: Duke Ellington School of the Arts
16thstreetheights.summary: A bassist raised in Petworth and Sixteenth Street Heights, where his parents encouraged his music. He started bass at ten, studied at Duke Ellington School of the Arts, and now tours with Kenny Garrett. He talks about gentrification and DC's jazz scene.
16thstreetheights.archive: Dig DC, DC Public Library (Jazz at Westminster Presbyterian Church)

archives.name: The People's Archive, DC Public Library
archives.how_to_search: Browse subject pages such as Petworth (subjects/835) or Tenleytown (subjects/965), or search collections like the DC Oral History Collaborative and Mapping Segregation projects; audio is accessed through Dig DC.

archives.name: Historic Chevy Chase DC Oral History Archive
archives.how_to_search: Browse the two-page oral history list; many Chevy Chase DC transcripts discuss Tenleytown, Fort Reno, Friendship Heights and Wilson High School.

archives.name: Humanities Truck Community Archive, American University
archives.how_to_search: Use the site search or browse the item list for Celebrate Petworth and Reno City collections.

archives.name: Tenleytown Historical Society
archives.how_to_search: Check the Oral History tag and the Reminiscence category under History.

archives.name: Boundary Stones (WETA)
archives.how_to_search: Search the blog by neighborhood name for local history pieces that draw on resident interviews.

archives.name: Glover Park History: Oral History and Reminiscences
archives.how_to_search: Browse the category list; each page credits its original source (Glover Park Gazette, Peabody Room, CAG or Naval Observatory oral history projects). The Streets category covers street-name history.

archives.name: Cleveland Park Historical Society Oral Histories
archives.how_to_search: Featured interviews have web transcripts; the 1984 Cleveland Park Voices interviews and later ones are linked as PDFs (the PDF host's robots.txt disallows automated fetching, so read them in a browser).

archives.name: Rainbow History Project Digital Collections
archives.how_to_search: Use Browse Items with a keyword such as 'Dupont Circle' or 'Adams Morgan' in the oral history collection; most audio is shared on request by email.

archives.name: hometown DC (DC History Center)
archives.how_to_search: Browse Explore Stories, which tags short video stories by ward.

archives.name: Hola Cultura: Adams Morgan History
archives.how_to_search: Video interviews and a bilingual keepsake on the Latino community in Adams Morgan.

archives.name: Citizens Association of Georgetown
archives.how_to_search: CAG runs the Georgetown Oral History Project; transcripts were not found on the current site, so contact CAG for access.

archives.name: Peabody Room, Georgetown Neighborhood Library (DC Public Library)
archives.how_to_search: Holds Georgetown oral histories such as the 1969 Raymond 'Kelly' Brown interview; ask the Peabody Room staff.

archives.name: Smithsonian Anacostia Community Museum Archives: A Right to the City Exhibition Records
archives.how_to_search: Includes oral histories tagged Adams Morgan; the site returned 403 to our crawler, so search it in a browser.

archives.name: Ruth Ann Overbeck Capitol Hill History Project
archives.how_to_search: Browse 200+ transcribed interviews alphabetically or filter by topic and time period; the site search finds street names and places in transcripts (try 'H Street NE').

archives.name: Mosaic Theater H Street Oral History Project
archives.how_to_search: Project page for interviews with H Street corridor residents; recordings are slated for DC Public Library's oral history collections.

archives.name: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division
archives.how_to_search: Holds the Michael Shiner diary (1813-1860s), a Navy Yard worker's first-person record; the Civil War in America exhibition biography introduces it.

archives.name: Anacostia Community Museum Archives (Smithsonian)
archives.how_to_search: Search the archives for Southwest DC and urban renewal oral histories. The site blocked our automated agent during research, so nothing here was checked or used.

archives.name: Naval History and Heritage Command, Navy Department Library
archives.how_to_search: Hosts a transcription of the Michael Shiner diary and Washington Navy Yard histories. The site would not connect for our agent, so nothing here was checked or used.

archives.name: The Catholic University of America Archives
archives.how_to_search: Its D.C. history guide lists Brookland collections such as the Brooks-Queen family papers, the Cecilia Parker Woodson letters and the Rose Society of Brookland minutes; no oral history series was found.

archives.name: Bygone Brookland
archives.how_to_search: Robert Malesky's Brookland history blog; browse the Brookland Roads category for street histories and reader recollections.

archives.name: Dig DC, DC Public Library
archives.how_to_search: Open the DC Oral History Collaborative collection and filter by neighborhood ('Southwest, Washington, D.C.' or 'Navy Yard, Washington, D.C.'), or browse the 'Southwest Remembered: A Story of Urban Renewal' (1983-85, 33 interviews) and Buzzard Point Oral History Project (2017, 9 interviews) collections. Search by keyword, then filter Object Type to Oral History Interview and use the Neighborhood facet (for example 'Noma/Sursum Corda' or 'Swampoodle'). The tags are loose, so read each abstract for a real tie.

archives.name: hometown DC (HumanitiesDC / Historical Society of Washington, D.C.)
archives.how_to_search: Browse the roughly 40 short clips; each is tagged with a ward.

archives.name: Dig DC, DC Public Library's digital repository
archives.how_to_search: Start at the DC Oral History Collaborative collection and its sub-collections (Chinatown Voices, Newton Street/The Cooperative at 1477, Stories of the Mott School in LeDroit Park); the U Street and South of U oral history projects are separate collections. Each interview page carries an abstract, date and running time.

archives.name: A Right to the City exhibition records, Anacostia Community Museum Archives (Smithsonian)
archives.how_to_search: The finding aid (PDF at sirismm.si.edu/EADpdfs/ACMA.03-119.pdf) lists about 100 2016-2018 interviews with Place tags for Chinatown, Shaw and Columbia Heights; each has an object page at anacostia.si.edu/collection/archives/object/sova-acma-03-119-refNN.

archives.name: Rainbow History Project Digital Collections
archives.how_to_search: Search for 'LCCA' to find the 2022 Logan Circle Community Association oral histories; audio is linked from each item or available by emailing the project.

archives.name: Palisades Community Association
archives.how_to_search: The About section holds the association's 1956/1966 community history. The DC Public Library's People's Archive also lists a Palisades oral history project (1999-2004) we could not read.

archives.name: Forest Hills Connection (neighborhood history series)
archives.how_to_search: Browse the Forest Hills History category for local history pieces on Van Ness, Grant Road and the Bureau of Standards; it is a community news site, not an archive.

archives.name: Foggy Bottom Association History Project: Oral Histories
archives.how_to_search: Short list under Watch, Listen and Read, with transcripts of the GWU Oral History Program interviews (1997) and the 2011 Briscoe and Riley interview. The GW Digital DC recordings are linked only through an archived copy, which we did not use.

archives.name: George Washington University Special Collections Research Center
archives.how_to_search: The Foggy Bottom Association's site is the lead for this oral history collection of long-time GW-area residents. The finding aid returned an empty challenge page to our agent, so nothing here was read or used.

archives.name: Woodley Park Community: A Sketch of Our Past
archives.how_to_search: A chapter history from the Woodley Park Community Association that quotes resident interviews from 1992 and 1993. Check the notes at the end of each chapter for who was interviewed.

archives.name: Empower DC: Ivy City
archives.how_to_search: Look under Learn about Ivy City History for the booklet, zines and audio documentary from its oral history project.

archives.name: Power of Preserving the Black Deaf Experience (Dig DC)
archives.how_to_search: Interviews in American Sign Language with former Kendall School students. Search 'Kendall School' and filter Object Type to Oral History Interview, or use the Gallaudet neighborhood facet.

archives.name: Gallaudet University Archives
archives.how_to_search: Holds Sandy White's research files on Black Deaf education and Kendall/Gallaudet. Search 'black deaf' in the finding aids.
